key_insight: Censored open-weight LLMs — models that withhold or suppress information for safety or policy reasons — provide a realistic, naturally-occurring testbed for studying secret-knowledge elicitation and lie-detection methods, revealing different failure modes than synthetically-trained lying models.
problem_solved: Prior evaluations use artificially constructed lying models that may not reflect real-world withholding behavior; this paper addresses the need for a more realistic benchmark to test methods that elicit truthful knowledge or detect falsehoods.
method: Collect and analyze open-weight LLMs that exhibit censorship/withholding behavior as a natural source of secret-knowledge scenarios.
Apply and compare honesty-elicitation techniques (prompt engineering, weight or decoding adjustments) to try to recover suppressed knowledge.
Train and evaluate lie-detection classifiers on model outputs to identify withheld or misleading responses and compare performance to synthetic lying-model baselines.
impact: Provides practitioners a more realistic evaluation framework for honesty and lie-detection techniques, improving robustness assessments and guiding safer deployment choices for models that intentionally withhold information.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 'Censored LLM' → elicitation prompts / methods → recovered vs withheld outputs (illustrates setup).
Bar chart comparing elicitation and detection performance on censored models vs synthetic lying models.
Example side-by-side prompt/output pairs showing successful and failed elicitation (before/after prompt tuning).
Heatmap or matrix of method effectiveness by type of censorship/policy and elicitation technique.
paper_title: Censored LLMs as a Natural Testbed for Secret Knowledge Elicitation
paper_authors: Helena Casademunt, Bartosz Cywiński, Khoi Tran, Arya Jakkli, Samuel Marks
